functions.evidence: Writes the identified OSMetaClass vtable, removes the class from sAllClassesDict and sStalled, releases its expansion allocation and poisons the vptr. Source: libkern/c++/OSMetaClass.cpp destructor.
Atomic increment of instanceCount at +0x24; on zero-to-one follows superClassLink at +0x10 and repeats. Native uses OSIncrementAtomic, original uses LDADD. Source: OSMetaClass.cpp:985.
Compares size x1 against the low 24 bits of ktv->kt_size at +0x2c, selects kalloc_type_impl_external with flags 4 or kalloc_ext, then accounts the allocation. Source: OSObject.cpp:312.
Null-checks x1, compares size x2 against ktv->kt_size at +0x2c, selects typed free or kfree_ext and subtracts size from allocation accounting. Source: OSObject.cpp:364.
Calls lck_rw_done, requires mode 1, otherwise panics with lck_rw_unlock_shared() and lock_rw_old.c. Native development image adds owner assertions before the same operation.
Calls lck_rw_done, requires mode 2, otherwise panics with lck_rw_unlock_exclusive() and lock_rw_old.c. Native development image adds owner assertions before the same operation.

Loads ktv->zone; delegates to kfree_type_impl_internal when registered. Otherwise selects the heap from kt_flags bits 0x8000 and 8, masks kt_size to 24 bits and tail-calls kfree_ext. Distinct from the IOFreeTypeImpl wrapper.
BTI plus tail branch to the separately identified kfree_type_impl_external. Source: iokit/Kernel/IOLib.cpp IOFreeTypeImpl; use the named native wrapper so its IOTRACKING behavior is retained.
Tests kt_flags bit 0x10 at +0x28, selects Z_ZERO=4 with or without Z_NOFAIL=0x8000, then calls kalloc_type_impl_external. Source: IOLib.cpp IOMallocTypeImpl.
Tags the view in x0 with bit 1 and calls kalloc_ext with size in x1, flags 0x1f1004 and null site. Source: IOLib.cpp IOMallocTypeVarImpl and kalloc_type_var_impl.
Tags the view in x0 with bit 1, preserves address x1 and size x2, then branches to kfree_ext. Source: IOLib.cpp IOFreeTypeVarImpl and kfree_type_var_impl.
Allocates from the same data heap selected by kfree_type_impl_external kt_flags bit 8, flags 0x31000, then accounts allocated bytes. Source: IOLib.cpp IOMallocData_external and IOMalloc_internal.
Same data-heap allocation path as IOMallocData_external, adding Z_ZERO=4 (0x31004). Source: IOLib.cpp IOMallocZeroData_external.
Null-checks the allocation, frees from the identified private data heap, then subtracts its size from IOKit allocation accounting. Source: IOLib.cpp IOFreeData and IOFree_internal.
Places current_thread()->thread_id in x5 (zero for null thread), zero in x6 and tail-calls kernel_debug_internal. Source: bsd/kern/kdebug.c kernel_debug; kernel_debug1 instead preserves caller x5.

Reads cpu_data through the current thread, snapshots cpu_timebase at +0x58 around the hardware counter read, retries if changed, then returns counter+offset. Native uses generic CNTVCT_EL0 plus ISB instead of Apple ACNTVCT, and its generated thread->cpu_data offset. This selects the hardware-independent native timebase algorithm.
Reorders caller name/buffer/length into x1/x2/x3, obtains PE_state.bootArgs->CommandLine at +0x6c and passes allow_prefix=0 to the parser. Native obtains the same buffer through PE_boot_args.

Variadic serial printer: disable_serial_output and disable_kprintf_output flags, interrupt masking, serial-output lock, console CPU tracking and a doprnt callback. Native _kprintf has the same flag/lock/callback sequence; the interrupt debug string is from an inlined helper, not the function identity.

Variadic console printer: stack guard, null-format check, console buffer initialized with state 3, doprnt, conditional console buffer flush, returns zero. Native _printf has the same console buffer protocol. Distinct from serial kprintf.

Checks preemption/can-sleep, increments thread rwlock count, atomically sets WANT_EXCL=0x80000 when state mask 0xdffff is clear, otherwise calls exclusive slow path; finally writes owner ctid. Source: lock_rw_old.c exclusive lock path.

Checks preemption/can-sleep, increments thread rwlock count, atomically increments reader count when state mask 0xd0000 is clear; otherwise tail-calls the shared slow path. Source: lock_rw_old.c shared lock path.

Writes the class-identified OSObject vtable with PACDA and initializes retainCount at +8 to 1. The protected constructor ignores its metaclass argument, as confirmed in OSObject.cpp. Both native overloads perform these same operations.
Poisons vptr with all ones and returns. Native OSObject base destructor delegates to OSMetaClassBaseD2, which performs the same poison operation; distinct from virtual deleting destruction and free.

Protected IOService constructor writes the class-identified IOService vtable and initializes inherited retainCount=1. It does not increment instanceConstructed; therefore map to C2(const OSMetaClass*), not C2(), whose native implementation increments the class instance count.

Base IOService destructor only poisons vptr. Native delegates through IORegistryEntryD2/OSObjectD2 to OSMetaClassBaseD2. Class identity comes from IOService structor call sites and the adjacent protected constructor; not the deleting destructor.

Locks vnode, increments its hold count with overflow checking, calls vnode_put_internal_locked(vp,0), then vnode_drop_internal(vp,1) and returns zero. Source: bsd/vfs/vfs_subr.c vnode_put, not vnode_hold (which was inlined).
Loads vnode.v_mount at +0xd8 and authenticates with address diversity 0xd6ef; returns zero for null. Native has the same field and discriminator, adding an explicit authentication failure trap.
Loads IOLockGroup then tail-calls mutex allocation; IOLocks.cpp IOLockAlloc passes LCK_ATTR_NULL, optimized away in the source RELEASE implementation.
Destroys mutex with IOLockGroup then frees the typed mutex allocation. Native delegates both operations to lck_mtx_free, matching IOLocks.cpp IOLockFree.
Checks thread owner at +0x18, increments recursion count at +0x20 for its owner, otherwise acquires the mutex and sets owner/count. Native uses the same offsets and adds DEVELOPMENT assertions.
Decrements recursion count at +0x20; on zero clears owner at +0x18 and releases the mutex. Native checks owner then performs these same operations.

Nonzero member pointer x1 is authenticated with type discriminator 0xa83d and resigned with function discriminator 0x4a27. Native uses the same PAC keys and discriminators, plus an explicit authentication failure trap. Source: OSMetaClass.cpp feature ptrauth_member_function_pointer_type_discrimination.

Stores the current hardware timebase plus cpu_timebase into the caller-provided uint64 pointer. Native invokes mach_absolute_time then performs that store. Source: osfmk/kern/clock.c clock_get_uptime.

Multiplies the two uint32 arguments into nanoseconds, converts to absolute time via the timebase, adds current absolute time with saturation and writes the third argument. Native calls the corresponding conversion and mach_absolute_time then performs saturating addition.

Converts hardware timebase plus cpu offset into seconds and microseconds, stores 64-bit seconds at +0 and 32-bit microseconds at +8. Native clock_get_system_microtime plus these stores implements bsd/kern/kern_time.c microuptime.
Passes event x0, false in w1 and THREAD_AWAKENED=0 in w2 to thread_wakeup_prim. Exact native _wakeup sequence and bsd/kern/kern_synch.c wrapper.

Complete 66-instruction body equals native sysctl_handle_long after address relocation: 32/64-bit sysctl output, signed truncation ERANGE check, optional new-value input. Shared body identity is ambiguous to the automatic unique-shape matcher; the reviewed sysctl handler preserves the exact behavior and ABI.

Masks vfs context thread tag bit 0, obtains its BSD task when present, otherwise returns current_thread_ro()->tro_proc or kernproc. Native vfs_context_proc performs the same selection with the current_proc fallback outlined.
Tail-calls current_thread_ro, matching native vfs_context_current and bsd/vfs/vfs_subr.c current VFS context representation.
Returns context.vc_ucred at +8, matching native vfs_context_ucred and the vfs_context structure.
Initializes the type/group header with 0x22000000, zeroes mutex state and references the lock group. Native lck_mtx_init performs the same initialization plus DEVELOPMENT-only lock-attribute checks.

Initializes the legacy RW lock layout with sleep/debug flag bits 2/0x40 and the lock-group RW count. Match the C _lck_rw_init from lock_rw_old.c, not the C++ overload that uses a different state encoding.
Adds the proc-to-task allocation offset to proc pointer, returning it only when proc flags bit 1 is set. Native uses its own proc flag offset and proc_struct_size global with the same algorithm.
Returns debug-enabled global, and if argument is nonnull writes the debug flags when enabled or zero otherwise. Native implements the same branch and adds an initialization assertion.
Obtains the current thread through TPIDR_EL1 and tail-calls get_threadtask; native outlines current_act but uses the same get_threadtask API.

Initializes retainCount=1 and writes the independently class-identified IOUserClient vtable. No instanceConstructed call: protected metaclass constructor. Native delegates to protected IOService constructor then writes the same class vtable.

Initializes retainCount=1 and writes the independently class-identified IOUserClient2022 vtable without instanceConstructed. Native protected metaclass constructor delegates to IOService then installs its class vtable.

Base IOUserClient destructor adjacent to its class-identified protected constructor writes all ones into vptr. Native IOUserClientD2 delegates through the base destructors to the same vptr poison operation, without deleting storage.

Preserves matching dictionary and timeout, supplies a null check-in token as third argument, and tail-calls the identified waitForMatchingServiceWithToken. Native overload has that same public signature.

Converts the char string using OSSymbol::withCString and withString, creates/updates a dictionary under IOProviderClass, and releases the temporary symbols. Uses the raw dictionary overload; native char-string overload performs the same ownership sequence.

Seventh-from-last of the lck_mtx_gate_* run between gate_wait and lck_mtx_gate_wait; no calls, initializes the gate words. Source order osfmk/kern/locks.c: init, alloc_init, destroy, free, try_close, close, open, handoff, steal, wait.
Calls kalloc_type_impl_internal then initializes; second in the lck_mtx_gate_* source order (osfmk/kern/locks.c).
Takes the gate bit lock (hw_lock_bit_to_contended) and checks the gate is unused; third in lck_mtx_gate_* source order.
Destroys the gate as destroy does, then kfree_type_impl_internal; fourth in lck_mtx_gate_* source order.
Gate bit lock with a non-blocking owner check; fifth in lck_mtx_gate_* source order.
Inlined gate_close (gate bit lock, owner set); sixth in lck_mtx_gate_* source order.
Tail call to gate_open; seventh in lck_mtx_gate_* source order.
Tail call to gate_handoff; eighth in lck_mtx_gate_* source order.
Tail call to gate_steal; ninth in lck_mtx_gate_* source order, directly before lck_mtx_gate_wait.
Body is bti; mov w0,#0; ret. Release code folding merged identical return-false functions; the native pmap_in_ppl has the same body, so every caller keeps the original result.

Body is bti; mov w0,#0; ret (folded return-false). Bound to a native function with the identical body so the original result 0 is kept; the native DEVELOPMENT kern_config_is_development returns 1 and must not be used.
Returns one 64-bit global (adrp/ldr #0x270); same shape as native ml_get_wake_timebase loading wake_abstime; sits between cpu_number and cpuid_get_cpufamily as in osfmk/arm64/machine_routines.c.
Reads the current thread kernel stack bounds from TPIDR_EL1 and returns sp minus the stack base (interrupt stack when on it). Source: osfmk/arm64/machine_routines.c ml_stack_remaining.
Same calls as the reference task_deallocate: os_ref release with os_ref_panic_underflow and task_deallocate_internal; directly after task_reference.
Locks the reporter (hw_lock with interrupts disabled), calls the per-channel update and unlocks; called from IOService::updateReport; same call set as the reference IOReporter::updateReport.
Returns the process text vnode after vnode_getwithref; same call as the reference proc_getexecutablevnode.
Allocates a callout record with zalloc_permanent and links it onto the kdp callout list; same call as the reference kdp_register_callout.
Calls req->oldfunc (SYSCTL_OUT of arg1/arg2), then req->newfunc when req->newptr is set (SYSCTL_IN). Source: bsd/kern/kern_newsysctl.c sysctl_handle_opaque.
Panics with '%s: function not supported in this environment' naming pmap_claim_reserved_ppl_page.
Panics with '%s: function not supported in this environment' naming pmap_free_reserved_ppl_page.
Stores the 32-bit address and length unswapped at segments[index] and returns true; OutputHost32 and OutputLittle32 have this body on a little-endian host (folded).
Stores the 64-bit address and length unswapped at segments[index] and returns true; OutputHost64 and OutputLittle64 have this body on a little-endian host (folded).

Called from kernel_bootstrap and returns the code signing monitor type and configuration flags (reads the configuration globals). The native implementation reports the native configuration without a monitor, which is what the original components must see on this kernel.
kern_codesigning.c source order between secure_channel_shared_page and developer_mode_state; TXM wrapper in original, XNU body in native
kern_codesigning.c source order after enable_developer_mode, before developer_mode_state
kern_codesigning.c source order after research_mode_state (0xfffffe000ad169dc)
kern_codesigning.c source order after extended_research_mode_state
kern_codesigning.c source order after restricted_execution_mode_enable
kern_codesigning.c source order after restricted_execution_mode_state
kern_codesigning.c source order after update_csm_device_state

Decrements gate->gt_refs, stores the GATE_DESTROYED poison, and calls gate_verify_tag_panic, gate_destroy_panic, gate_destroy_owned_panic and gate_destroy_waiter_panic; internal helper of osfmk/kern/locks.c gate_destroy_internal.
Clears the per-CPU SMR tracker with stlr xzr at base + index * 128, then balances the preemption-disable counter; osfmk/kern/smr.c smr_leave.
Returns upl[index].phys_addr != 0; osfmk/vm/vm_pageout.c upl_page_present.
Tests bit 2 (dirty) of the UPL flags word after the phys_addr check; vm_pageout.c upl_dirty_page.
Returns the inverse of bit 1 (absent) of the UPL flags word; vm_pageout.c upl_valid_page.
Table lookup of kern_return_t returning EIO above 56; osfmk/kern/bsd_kern.c mach_to_bsd_errno.
Builds vnop_getxattr_args and calls v_op[vnop_getxattr_desc.vdesc_offset]; bsd/vfs/kpi_vfs.c VNOP_GETXATTR.
Inlined bawrite_internal(bp, 1): vnode_waitforwrites with VNODE_ASYNC_THROTTLE and the buf_bawrite message, sets B_ASYNC, then VNOP_BWRITE; bsd/vfs/vfs_bio.c.
Compares the MPIDR cluster of the target with this CPU and writes S3_5_C15_C0_0 or S3_5_C15_C0_1 with the immediate IPI type; ml_cpu_signal with ml_cpu_signal_type inlined.
Follows vp->v_mount->mnt_vnodecovered without taking the mount lock; bsd/vfs/kpi_vfs.c.
Returns proc->p_textvp without proc lock; bsd/kern/kern_proc.c.
Rejects types outside FSE_MAX_EVENTS with no watcher and VT_DEVFS vnodes; bsd/vfs/vfs_fsevents.c need_fsevent.
Returns csb_csm_trust_level when the monitor object exists, otherwise UINT32_MAX; bsd/kern/kern_cs.c.
Validates the authenticated queue magic, data and size against the ring fields and stores the entry; iokit/IOKit/IOCircularDataQueueImplementation.h.
Entry thunk into the csm_free_provisioning_profiles walk under profiles_lock; with a monitor this frees unreferenced profiles, the software backend has none.
bti, dsb sy, ret: iokit/IOKit/IOService.cpp OSSynchronizeIO.
Authenticates the thread_ro pointer, returns thread_ro->allocation_name and stores the new value only when the field is empty; osfmk/kern/thread.c thread_set_allocation_name.
Strips the PAC bits, applies the slid/permuted address ranges and returns the hidden address through the out pointer; osfmk/vm/vm_kern.c vm_kernel_addrhide.
Loads CpuDataEntries[cpu].cpu_data_vaddr and applies PERCPU_GET_RELATIVE(processor, cpu_data, cpu_data); osfmk/arm/cpu_common.c cpu_to_processor.
Passes the varargs, reason, context and debugger mask to panic_trap_to_debugger; the exclaves watchdog request is compiled out in the software backend; osfmk/kern/debug.c panic_with_options.
Returns the 32-bit process group id field at proc+0x24; bsd/kern/kern_proc.c proc_pgrpid.
Copies proc->p_syscall_filter_mask into the caller buffer with the size and null checks of kern_proc.c proc_get_syscall_filter_mask.
Switches on CL_READ/CL_WRITE, reads mnt_seg/read/write counts, clamps to the UPL size and returns the byte maximum; bsd/vfs/vfs_cluster.c cluster_max_io_size.
Builds vnop_fsync_args with vnop_fsync_desc and calls the vnode operation; bsd/vfs/kpi_vfs.c VNOP_FSYNC.
Builds vnop_strategy_args with vnop_strategy_desc and calls the vnode operation; bsd/vfs/kpi_vfs.c VNOP_STRATEGY.
Returns ~((1 << page_shift) - 1) from map->page_shift, with PAGE_SHIFT when the map is null; osfmk/vm/vm_map.c vm_map_page_mask.
Locks the socket, calls pru_sockaddr through pr_usrreqs, copies out the address; bsd/kern/kpi_socket.c sock_getsockname.
Apple TXM stub panics unsupported; replaced by the software backend that returns the static Image4 storage area and its size (bsd/kern/code_signing/xnu.c).

Fast path is a compare-swap of 0 to the cpu number at lock+8, i.e. the mutex data word; lck_spin_t keeps its data at +0 and its type at +8, so this body is a mutex lock, not a spin lock (the earlier lck-spin label read the same CAS shape). Corecrypto allocates the mutex with lck_mtx_alloc_init and locks it here.
Try-lock of the same mutex data word at lock+8, returning whether it was acquired. Same layout argument as lck_mtx_lock.
Compare-swap releases the mutex data word at lock+8 back to zero, matching lck_mtx_unlock; a spin unlock would release the word at lock+0.

Copies the 8-byte timebase value at __DATA+8 into *x0 and returns. Native _clock_timebase_info is the same five-instruction getter reading gTimebaseInfo; only the adrp/add constants differ, so neither body-hash nor shape can pair it. corecrypto's tick-to-time conversions call it at 0xa6d2844 and eighteen more sites; panic IMG_20261030_090251.jpg returned from 0xa6d2848 with the out-parameter on the stack.

Loads panic_state at __DATA+0xcb4 and returns (state - 3) < 2 with cset. Native _panic_active has the identical body; only the state slot address differs. Called from corecrypto at 0xa6e171c and 0xa6e17b8.

Claim-once registration: returns -1 when the pointer slot at __DATA+0xaf0 is already set, else stores the argument there, sets the byte at +0xae8 and returns 0. Native _register_crypto_functions runs the same sequence with its own slot offsets. Called from corecrypto at 0xa72d4a4.

entropy_init(64, entropyseed), stores ctx in prng_ctx, copies cckprng_funcs while authenticating each slot with the same discriminators as native (0x6961/0xf60a/0x5d01/0x4d5f/0xedeb/0x3051), then four cc_clear scrubs. Native _register_and_init_prng is the same sequence plus inline boot_cpu/prng_ready asserts. Source: osfmk/prng/prng_random.c; called from corecrypto at 0xa72dc28.

prng_funcs.refresh(prng_ctx) (discriminator 0x4d5f) then the generate loop in 0x100-byte chunks (discriminator 0xedeb) with cpu_number read from tpidr_el1. Native _read_random runs the same sequence; the native build calls cpu_number instead of inlining it. Called from corecrypto at 0xa708e50.

kalloc_type of the lock, tag 0x22000000|flags into the new object, then references the lock group (donor inlines the group reference; the RELEASE reference build calls _lck_grp_reference). Our reference build orders _lck_mtx_alloc_init immediately before _lck_mtx_init with that same body. Called from corecrypto at 0xa713910 right after lck_grp_alloc_init.

strlen(arg1)+1, then req->oldfunc, then the req->newfunc path with the truncating store, i.e. the reference build's _sysctl_handle_string byte for byte except that the donor build authenticates the function pointers with string discriminators (0x6827) and hardens the store address with a PAC'd pointer; it also sits between sysctl_handle_long and sysctl_handle_opaque in the donor order. Source: bsd/kern/kern_sysctl.c.

AppleImage4 calls it as (static kalloc_type_view in __DATA_CONST 0x7f64320, zflags 4) during early init; body builds KT_VIEW flags 0xd001000|(flags&7), reads ktv view fields at +0/+8/+40, indexes the per-cpu zone array at cpu<<14 (cpu from tpidr_el1+424) and tail-calls zalloc_ext with (zone, size&0xffffff, flags). Source order in kalloc.c sits exactly between _kalloc_data_require and _kalloc_type_var_impl (= kalloc_type_impl_external at kalloc.c:2720); our native body at 0x7334c20 has the same 0xd001000|flags construction and [x0] null-check. First live call site 0xfffffff008d419e8 was the fileset unmapped-call diagnostic of the r83 boot.

One int arg, two-sided free-slot scan over bdevsw[] at 0xb2ebf70 (stride 0x38 = sizeof(struct bdevsw)): -1 starts at 1 (volfs collision avoidance), other negatives start at -index, memcmp against the nobdev template at 0x7d5f438 (56 bytes) and returns the index or -1; forward bound cmp 0x17 = nblkdev-1. Source: bsd/kern/bsd_stubs.c bdevsw_isfree. IOStorageFamily registers its media device from here; first live call 0xfffffff009f84d8c passed w0=-1 and fired the fileset unmapped-call diagnostic of the batchfix boot (crc 0x20c30dfb).

Two args (index, const struct bdevsw *): devsw_lock_list_mtx spin lock (tpidr_el1+0x1b8 counter + casa on 0xb418c00), inlined bdevsw_isfree scan over the 0x38-stride table, then ldp q0/q1 + ldr q2 copies the 56-byte bdevsw into the slot. Source: bsd/kern/bsd_stubs.c bdevsw_add.

Two args (index, const struct bdevsw *): bounds cmp 0x17 (nblkdev-1), entry = bdevsw+index*0x38, devsw_lock_list_mtx lock, memcmp against the caller's bsw and on match restores nobdev. Donor IOStorageFamily calls it to roll the bdevsw_add back when cdevsw_add_with_bdev fails. Source: bsd/kern/bsd_stubs.c bdevsw_remove.

Two args (index, const struct cdevsw *): devsw_lock_list_mtx lock, inlined cdevsw_isfree scan, copies the caller's csw into cdevsw[] (0x70 = sizeof(struct cdevsw) stride, table at 0xb2ec4b0). Donor inlines cdevsw_isfree here, so it is absent as a separate donor function. Source: bsd/kern/bsd_stubs.c cdevsw_add. Internal callee of donor cdevsw_add_with_bdev (0xfffffe000ae3f70c).

Two args (index, const struct cdevsw *): memcmp against the caller's csw on the 0x70-stride cdevsw[] table and on match restores nocdev and clears cdevsw_flags[index]. Source: bsd/kern/bsd_stubs.c cdevsw_remove.

Three args (index, const struct cdevsw *csw, int bdev): calls cdevsw_add (0xfffffe000ae3f44c), bounds-checks the bdev major (cmp 0x17), re-verifies the cdevsw slot free at 0x70 stride and wires the chrtoblk mapping; on failure the caller rolls back with bdevsw_remove. Source: bsd/kern/bsd_stubs.c cdevsw_add_with_bdev.

Registry walk under the metaclass lock: first entry's virtual slot 0x128 resolves the name, unlock, then the object's getMetaClass (slot 0x38) and a super-chain walk via [meta+0x10]; 0x154 bytes between donor checkMetaCast(OSMetaClassBase) and metaCast(const char*). Source: libkern/c++/OSMetaClass.cpp checkMetaCastWithName(const OSSymbol*, const OSMetaClassBase*).

The delegating OSMetaClass constructor: base ctor call, gIOKitDebug flag-byte check bit 6, then zone_create(zone_name=x5, size=x3, flags|x6 orr #0x2000000 = ZC_ZFREE_CLEARMEM, 0xffff, 0) stored into *zone=x4. AMFI calls it from its class constructor with (this, className, super, 0x28, &zone, zoneName, flags); the returned pointer gets a pacda x17(0xcda1)-signed vtable store. Source: libkern/c++/OSMetaClass.cpp OSMetaClass(inClassName, inSuperClass, inClassSize, inZone, zone_name, zflags). Live call site 0xfffffff008f1b14c fired the kernconf-boot wall (crc 0xbfe4144d).

Shape-identical to our native allocClassWithName(const OSString*): OSSymbol::withString(x0) (its OSDynamicCast against gOSSymbolMetaClass with retain-or-construct via flags bit 0 kOSStringNoCopy is donor 0xfffffe000ae7fcac, paired), then allocClassWithName(const OSSymbol*) (donor 0xfffffe000ae42928, paired), then release the temp symbol through virtual slot 0x28 and return the alloc result. Source: libkern/c++/OSMetaClass.cpp.

Same wrapper as our native allocClassWithName(const char*): OSSymbol::withCStringNoCopy(x0) (donor 0xfffffe000ae7fd88, strnlen against kMaxStringLength 0x3fffe, paired), then allocClassWithName(const OSSymbol*) (donor 0xfffffe000ae42928, paired), release temp, return result. Source: libkern/c++/OSMetaClass.cpp.
bti c; ldr x0, [x0, #0x10]; ret — identical to our native getSuperClass; the same +0x10 super link is walked by donor checkMetaCastWithName (0xfffffe000ae40a90). Source: libkern/c++/OSMetaClass.cpp.

OSObject::operator new: gIOKitDebug flag-byte check bit 6, then kalloc_type(OSObject name at 0x7d62688, size=x0, flags 0x4001004, 0) and an atomic instance-count bump (ldadd) at the gOSObject counter; donor order sits directly before _OSObject_typed_operator_new (reviewed), exactly like our native operator new at 0x7a201f8. Source: libkern/c++/OSObject.cpp.

count at [x0+0x14], PAC'd array at [x0+0x20] (disc 0xfeb9), scans slots from index w2 comparing raw [x1] pointers and returns the index or -1 — byte-shape identical to our native OSArray::getNextIndexOfObject at 0x7a21e38. Source: libkern/c++/OSArray.cpp.
count==0 returns NULL, else array[count-1] with the same PAC'd array (disc 0xfeb9) — byte-shape identical to our native OSArray::getLastObject at 0x7a21df8. Source: libkern/c++/OSArray.cpp.

os_log_create(subsystem, category): AMFI calls it with ('com.apple.MobileFileIntegrity', 'library_validation_failure') at 0xfffffff008f0dfd0 and falls back to a cached default handle via csel when it returns NULL (crc 0x88a9cb7 boot). Donor body sits in donor order between _os_log_equ and __os_log_internal and reads the CNTVCT-class register for the log timestamp; our native _os_log_create at 0x7a66f78 is the only candidate in that interval. Twelve call sites across AppleARMPlatform/AppleMobileFileIntegrity/IOAVFamily/IOHIDFamily/sandbox.

20-byte tail thunk: bti c; adrp the lock-group global at 0xb375058; ldr x0; mov x1,#0; b the rw-lock allocator (donor 0xfffffe000a7f4a44, itself paired).
